I am 58 years old with no schooling, and this 0.81 hectare plot is rented, so I am careful not to waste money on costly inputs I cannot recover. In Tabora, the rains come once a year, and I have always grown my food crops with what the land and my family can provide. I will plant using local cuttings or seed saved from last season, spread manure from my few cattle to keep the soil soft, and work the plot with my family using hand hoes as we have always done. Chemical fertilizer, pesticides, and irrigation are things for richer farmers or those growing cotton and tobacco, not for a man like me renting land to feed his household.
